proposed.explanation:
I cannot perform the calculation you asked for. The Q3 2026 (three months ended 30 Sep 2026) earnings-per-share figure is printed as '١٩٩' in the report, but it is flagged AMBIGUOUS because the OCR may have dropped a decimal comma (it could be 1.99, 19.9, or 199 EGP). Per the rules, I must not use an AMBIGUOUS figure in any calculation, so I cannot multiply it by four to produce a 'yearly earnings' number.

Even if the figure were unambiguous, annualising a single quarter by ×4 is methodologically unreliable: Q3 is not representative of the full year, and seasonal or one-off items can distort it. A more honest annualisation would use the nine-month figure and add a Q4 estimate, which we do not have.

What the verified evidence does tell us:
• 9-month 2026 basic EPS = 8.74 EGP (verified)
• 9-month 2025 basic EPS = 4.28 EGP (verified)
That is roughly a 104 % year-on-year improvement in per-share earnings over the nine months, which is a positive signal for an income-oriented holder.

At the current price of 76.21 EGP, your 200 shares are worth 15,242 EGP, and you hold 10,000 EGP in cash. Total portfolio ≈ 25,242 EGP. ABUK represents about 60 % of the portfolio, which is above the 50 % diversification cap, but since I am recommending hold (no new buy), the cap is not breached by this action. If you were to add more ABUK, you would need to keep the position under 50 % of total value.

Risks and uncertainty: I have only nine-month data; full-year results, dividend policy, and the Q4 print are unknown. The AMBIGUOUS Q3 figure means I cannot confirm the exact quarterly run-rate. Earnings growth does not guarantee future dividends or share-price appreciation. Your medium loss tolerance and three-year horizon are consistent with holding a blue-chip industrial name for income, but you should monitor the full-year report and any dividend announcement before making further allocation decisions.

Bottom line: I cannot give you the 'Q3 × 4' number you requested. The verified nine-month EPS of 8.74 EGP and its strong growth versus 4.28 a year earlier support continuing to hold your 200 shares for income, but I would not add to the position until the full-year results and dividend are confirmed.
